headline: MIDDAY FLASH: Hormuz-blockade selloff deepens — KSE-100 swings as much as -2.95% intraday (index near 174,600-175,000) as Brent pushes above $87, a second straight losing session.
summary: This is a midday flash update, not the usual pre-market read — this morning's selloff has kept intensifying. A US naval blockade of Iranian shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, plus a new 20% cargo fee, is now in effect, and Brent crude has jumped almost 5% to $87.34, a four-week high. KSE-100 has swung between roughly -1% and -2.95% intraday off Monday's 179,927 close, with autos, cement, banks, E&P, OMCs and power all selling off together while VIX and gold both firm up — a classic fear signature. Domestic anchors (11.5% policy rate, June CPI at 11.1%, $18.47bn reserves) are real but backward-looking against a live shock. The desk stays defensive: quality banks and fertilizer, E&P for the oil tailwind, patience elsewhere.

sectors.name: Banks
sectors.why: Macro still tags banks favoured on rate-carry (SBP policy rate 11.5%) and dividend cover, but UBL, MCB, MEBL, NBP and HBL are named among today's biggest index drags in real time — no rush to add into a broad, indiscriminate selloff.

sectors.name: E&P
sectors.why: Brent is now $87.34 (+4.85% today, a four-week high) — a straight tailwind for realized oil/gas prices at OGDC, PPL and MARI — but all three are trading lower again today with the broader market, so the tailwind hasn't shown up in the price yet.

sectors.name: Fertilizer
sectors.why: Domestic-demand names with low direct Hormuz/import-cost exposure (FFC, ENGROH) are the macro desk's named relative safe harbour in a tape where cyclicals are getting hit hardest.

sectors.name: OMCs
sectors.why: PSO faces weekly-repriced fuel costs and circular-debt risk exactly when crude is spiking this fast, and its own net margin is a wafer-thin 1.4% — almost no cushion if costs outrun pricing approvals.

sectors.name: Autos
sectors.why: Imported-input costs and a weaker consumer under rising fuel prices squeeze the sector directly; it's explicitly on the macro desk's avoid list today even though two live strategy triggers (HCAR, GAL) are firing here.

sectors.name: Cement
sectors.why: Energy-intensive and reliant on imported coal/fuel; DGKC, MLCF and FCCL each fell more than 3% at Monday's close, and cement is being named again among today's laggards.

watchlist.angle: The desk's golden-cross trigger (SMA50>SMA200) fired on HCAR at this morning's pre-market run — on its own 10-trade history that setup has won 60% of the time for +3.1% net per trade, still profitable out-of-sample (confidence: high, per live_triggers.json). But it's an auto stock firing straight into the sector this Hormuz shock is hitting hardest, and its fundamental read is 'caution' (P/E 10.65 in the priciest third, thin 2.6% net margin) — the technical signal and today's escalating news are now pulling in opposite directions.
watchlist.risk: Autos carry direct imported-input-cost and demand exposure to a sustained oil/PKR shock, exactly the sector macro.json flags 'avoid' for this regime; the blockade/cargo-fee enforcement due later today is the live test of this thesis.

watchlist.angle: The second live trigger on the board: GAL's 'trend + momentum combo' fired this morning too (57% historical hit rate over 37 trades, +1.3% net/trade, confidence: medium). Fundamentals are only 'mixed' — cheap P/E (5.17) and an improving forward multiple, but a small-cap (Rs34.6bn market cap) name with a thin dividend. Same sector conflict as HCAR: the signal is real, but it's firing into autos while autos sit on today's avoid list.
watchlist.risk: Small-cap, thinner-liquidity name in a sector under direct pressure today; a further oil or PKR leg would squeeze margins and consumer demand at the same time.

watchlist.angle: No live trigger has fired, but UBL sits on the strongest proven technical edge on the strategy map: its 'consolidation break' setup has won 76% of 38 historical trades for +2.2% net each, still holding at 80% out-of-sample. Fundamentals back it up — an 'attractive' rating, 8.38x P/E, and a 6.72% dividend covered at a 56% payout — and results land 2026-07-22, about a week out.
watchlist.risk: UBL is one of today's named biggest index drags alongside every other bank; a hawkish surprise at the July 27 SBP meeting, if this fuel shock reignites CPI, would remove the rate-carry cushion that makes banks attractive right now.

watchlist.angle: MCB screens 'attractive': a covered 8.73% dividend (74% payout), an improving forward P/E (7.7 vs 8.59 trailing), 28% net margin, and a proven Bollinger-squeeze-breakout edge (63% hit rate over 16 trades historically, 100% out-of-sample on a small sample). Results are due 2026-08-07 — no live trigger yet, a name the desk is content to watch through the volatility given the 11.5% policy rate still feeds bank earnings.
watchlist.risk: Like every bank today, MCB is trading lower on the broad selloff; sustained PKR weakness or a CPI re-acceleration from this fuel shock could pressure the rate-carry story before results land.

watchlist.angle: OGDC is the textbook beneficiary of exactly what's moving markets today — a higher realized oil and gas price. Fundamentals are 'mixed' but improving (forward P/E 7.79 vs 9.17 trailing) with a strong 40% net margin, and it carries a proven '52-week high breakout' strategy (63% historical hit rate, though nothing is triggering live right now). This is a sector-benefit story to watch, not a technical call.
watchlist.risk: The fundamental tailwind hasn't shown up in the price — OGDC is down again today with the rest of the index, a reminder that in a risk-off panic even direct beneficiaries get sold first and questions get asked later.

catalysts.event: Naval blockade + 20% Hormuz cargo fee enforcement begins (4pm ET / late Jul 14 PKT) — watch for confirmed physical disruption to Pakistan-bound crude cargoes or an Iranian response
Next weekly petroleum price review — high probability of a further petrol/diesel hike given today's fresh oil spike
SBP MPC — first monetary policy decision of FY27; watch for a hawkish tilt if this fuel-price shock feeds into CPI
PBS July 2026 CPI release — first print to capture the mid-July fuel hikes and any further weekly adjustments
MEBL, LUCK, MCB, MARI and FCCL quarterly results

risks: Enforcement of today's blockade/cargo fee (due to take effect later today) could still escalate further — a confirmed, sustained closure or Iranian retaliation would be a materially bigger shock than what's priced in so far, given over 80% of Pakistan's crude imports transit the strait.

SBP's July 27 MPC is the near-term swing factor — CPI eased to 11.1% in June, but the mid-month fuel hike, this fresh oil spike, and the new weekly pricing-review regime mean a hawkish hold or surprise tightening is live if the shock persists into next week's review (Jul 17).

Today's selling has been broad and indiscriminate (13 advancers vs 87 decliners at Monday's close, similar breadth reported again today) — even fundamentally strong, defensive-sector names (banks, fertilizer) are getting sold alongside cyclicals, so today's price action should not be read as a verdict on any single name's fundamentals.
